## Prima Content

But these are something else entirely: entirely hallucinated tomes of gibberish based on plagiarizing online information about a game. And it’s a smart con, too, given Amazon’s propensity to promote associated items if you’ve pre-ordered a copy of any of these games. At $20 or more, it’s not a cheap trick to fall for, too. The cover images are pretty convincing at a glance, and a parent looking to pick up a kid a gift, or just a regular games player having it show up in their Amazon recommendations, could very easily and innocently fall for it.
